title: The Narrator Who Leaves a Gap
fact_notes: オリジナル論説・架空事例。実在する企業、芸術作品、人物、調査結果ではない。台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A narrative can guide readers toward an understanding of events without providing a complete account of everything that happens within its fictional world.
sentences.ja: 物語は架空世界で起きるすべての完全な説明を提供せずに読者を出来事の理解へ導ける。

sentences.en: Readers frequently make inferences about actions, motives and relationships that are not described explicitly but that seem consistent with the information the narrative provides.
sentences.ja: 読者は明示的に描かれないが物語の提供情報と一致するように見える行動、動機、関係を頻繁に推論する。

sentences.en: The distinction between a detail that is absent from a text and an interpretation that is unsupported by it is consequently important.
sentences.ja: したがって本文にない細部と本文に支持されない解釈との区別は重要である。

sentences.en: A fictional narrative may leave certain matters uncertain while still offering readers grounds for accepting some interpretations more readily than others.
sentences.ja: 架空物語は一部事柄を不確かなまま残しつつ、他より受け入れやすい解釈の根拠を読者に提供することがある。

sentences.en: Consider an invented story in which a young musician receives an invitation to perform at an event that she has been hoping to attend for several months.
sentences.ja: 若い音楽家が数か月参加を望んでいた催しで演奏する招待を受ける創作物語を考えよう。

sentences.en: The narrator describes the character reading the message and preparing several possible replies, but the story does not immediately reveal which reply she eventually sends.
sentences.ja: 語り手は人物が連絡を読み返信案を複数準備する様子を描くが、物語は最終的にどの返信を送るか直ちに明らかにしない。

sentences.en: The following scene takes place several weeks later and presents the musician practicing in a room with another person whom the reader has not previously encountered.
sentences.ja: 次場面は数週間後で、音楽家が読者が以前出会っていない別人と部屋で練習する様子を示す。

sentences.en: Although the new scene provides evidence that the musician continues to pursue her interest, it does not by itself establish whether she has accepted the invitation.
sentences.ja: 新場面は音楽家が関心を追求し続ける証拠を提供するが、招待を承諾したかをそれだけで確定しない。

sentences.en: One reader assumes that the practice session is preparation for the event, interpreting the gap between the scenes as an omission of information that can readily be supplied.
sentences.ja: ある読者は練習を催しの準備と想定し、場面間の空白を容易に補える情報の省略と解釈する。

sentences.en: Another reader notices that earlier sections of the story described the musician's uncertainty about traveling to the event and considers the possibility that she has chosen a different activity.
sentences.ja: 別の読者は以前の箇所が催しに出向くことへの音楽家の不確かさを描いたと気づき、別活動を選んだ可能性を考える。

sentences.en: Both readers are attempting to connect events, but they rely upon different aspects of the information that the narrative makes available.
sentences.ja: 両読者とも出来事を結びつけようとしているが物語が提供する情報の異なる側面に依存する。

sentences.en: Their disagreement provides an opportunity to examine the evidence supporting each interpretation rather than merely deciding which account is more satisfying.
sentences.ja: 意見の不一致はどちらの説明がより満足できるか単に決めるのでなく各解釈を支える証拠を調べる機会を提供する。

sentences.en: The fact that a possible explanation would produce a coherent story does not establish that it is the only explanation compatible with the text.
sentences.ja: ある可能な説明が一貫した物語を生むという事実は、それが本文と両立する唯一の説明だと確定しない。

sentences.en: The fictional author could clarify the matter in a later scene, introducing information that would encourage readers to reconsider their earlier assumptions.
sentences.ja: 架空作者は後場面で事柄を明らかにし、読者が以前の前提を再考するよう促す情報を導入できる。

sentences.en: Alternatively, the story might continue without confirming which activity the musician selected, allowing attention to shift toward the significance of her continuing practice.
sentences.ja: 別の方法として音楽家がどの活動を選んだか確認せず物語が続き、練習を続ける意義へ注意を移せるかもしれない。

sentences.en: These possibilities would produce different relationships between the question left unanswered by the earlier scene and the questions that become relevant as the narrative develops.
sentences.ja: 可能性は以前場面の未解決問いと物語発展に伴い関連する問いの間に異なる関係を生む。

sentences.en: A reader's initial desire to resolve a particular uncertainty may therefore need to be distinguished from an assessment of the role that the uncertainty plays within the larger work.
sentences.ja: そこで特定の不確かさを解決したい読者の当初欲求は、大作品内で不確かさが果たす役割の評価と区別する必要があるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The reader may consequently need to revise not only an interpretation but also the question that initially guided it.
sentences.ja: したがって読者は解釈だけでなく当初その解釈を導いた問いも修正する必要があるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The interpretation of fiction can involve the recognition of limits as well as the discovery of connections.
sentences.ja: フィクションの解釈にはつながりの発見だけでなく限界の認識も伴い得る。

sentences.en: A gap in a narrative invites readers to consider possibilities, but it does not necessarily authorize them to treat their preferred explanation as a fact established by the text.
sentences.ja: 物語の空白は読者に可能性を考えるよう促すが、好ましい説明を本文に確立された事実と扱うことを必ずしも許さない。

sentences.en: Careful reading requires sensitivity to distinctions among what is stated, what is supported by inference and what remains genuinely unresolved.
sentences.ja: 注意深い読解には述べられたこと、推論により支持されること、本当に未解決のことの区別への感受性が必要だ。

sentences.en: A narrative can be rich in meaning precisely because it leaves some questions open.
sentences.ja: 物語はまさに一部の問いを開いたまま残すから意味に富み得る。

vocabulary.definition: part of a story or performance
connected in a clear and logical way

questions.prompt: What distinction is central to the opening?
options: All missing details necessarily make a story meaningless.
Fictional events cannot support any inference.
Missing details are not the same as unsupported interpretations.
Every reader must reach the same interpretation.
questions.explanation_ja: 描写の省略と根拠のない解釈。

questions.prompt: What does the story initially leave uncertain?
options: Whether she has ever played music.

questions.prompt: What does the second scene establish?
options: She has definitely accepted the invitation.
She continues practicing music, but her response to the invitation is uncertain.
The other person is the event organizer.

questions.prompt: What earlier information does the second reader consider?
options: The exact date of a confirmed performance.
A detailed description of the event venue.

questions.prompt: Why compare the two readers' explanations?
options: Both readers must invent new events freely.
Different interpretations depend on different textual evidence.
Only the most satisfying story is supported.
questions.explanation_ja: 依拠する根拠が異なる。

options: More than one coherent explanation may fit the text.
A text always states every cause of an event.
A satisfying interpretation is necessarily false.
questions.explanation_ja: 一貫性だけで唯一とは言えない。

questions.prompt: What could the author do instead of resolving the uncertainty?
options: Confirm that every interpretation is correct.
Continue the story while shifting attention to continued practice.

questions.prompt: Why might the reader's desire for resolution need reconsideration?
options: Every open question is a mistake by the author.
The gap may serve a different purpose in the larger narrative.
Readers should never seek textual evidence.
The story must answer all questions immediately.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: A story must explain every event to be meaningful.
Any possible interpretation should be treated as a fact.
Narrative gaps can enrich interpretation, but readers should distinguish supported inferences from unresolved matters.
The best reading always resolves every uncertainty.
questions.explanation_ja: 空白と根拠・不確かさ。

paraphrases.source: Their disagreement provides an opportunity to examine the evidence supporting each interpretation rather than merely deciding which account is more satisfying.
paraphrases.rewrite: The readers can examine evidence instead of choosing only the more satisfying explanation.
